runs.name: Ferrovial N.V.; Nasdaq FER, SEC CIK 0001468522, a 20-F filer reporting in euros under IFRS; an infrastructure group in Highways, Airports, Construction and Energy (407 ETR at 48.3% after a 5.06% purchase in June 2025, US managed lanes, New Terminal One at JFK, Budimex in Poland); the last 5.25% of Heathrow sold July 2025 and AGS Airports January 2025; Ferrovial SE converted to Ferrovial N.V. on 2026-04-30, delisted from Euronext Amsterdam effective 2026-09-11; the 20-F names no rival, the toll-road owners flagged as not SEC filers, Granite and Fluor read for construction as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q5; integrity, on doubt
runs.entry: Price **$49.41** a share (Nasdaq close 2026-10-16, `tools/sources.py`, aggregator, flagged), EUR **43.94** at EUR/USD 1.1244 (aggregator, flagged); the quote about $68 in June 2026, the fall not explained and not used. Shares **721,132,155** outstanding at 2026-06-30, one class (20-F cover 720,626,181 at 2025-12-31 via `Screens/cover_shares.py`, checked against issued 733,755,372 less treasury; 4,200,000 cancelled per 6-K 0001468522-26-000016; treasury 8,423,217 per the H1 2026 statements, 6-K 0001628280-26-050224; buybacks after June not counted); cap **EUR 31,689M** ($35,630M). Sovereign **3.67%** (ECB euro area AAA 30-year spot, 2026-10-15). Documents read: 20-F FY2025 (`0001628280-26-011789`; the 20-F/A `0001628280-26-064381` not needed), 20-F FY2024 (`0001468522-25-000034`), the 20-FR12B of 2024-01-05 (`0001104659-24-001882`) for FY2020 to FY2022, the H1 2026 report on 6-K, the 2026 6-Ks on I-24, I-285 East, the N.V. conversion, the Euronext delisting and the buybacks; FY2017 to FY2019 balance sheets from the company's own audited accounts on ferrovial.com (not SEC filings, flagged). Cross-check: FY2025 operating cash EUR 1,926M on the filed statement and as the sum of the Item 5.B columns. `tools/run.py` reads nothing for this IFRS filer; all arithmetic by hand in `q7.py`. The brief's one stated departure: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 4.B, 3.D and 5 of the FY2025 20-F (seven, listed in Step 0). The 20-F names no rival; the toll-road owners in the filings (Transurban, Meridiam, Vinci, ACS, Macquarie) flagged as not SEC filers; Granite and Fluor taken for construction margins as a CONVENTION of the run. **Q1 IN**, narrowly: Highways 74% of five-year adjusted EBIT (EUR 2,657M of 2021-25) plus EUR 452M of 407 ETR dividends in 2025, its economics written into concessions running to 2061-2098; NTO at JFK unforeseeable but not deciding. **Q2 IN on Highways** **[M2005-020]**, **[M2010-092]**, **[M2011-015]**: 407 ETR revenue compounding 8.3% a year since 2009, toll revenue +20.2% in H1 2026 on traffic +1.8%; US managed lanes revenue per trip up 9% to 19% against 2.7% inflation; Construction an open castle (operating margins 2021-25 Ferrovial 2.6%, Granite 3.4%, Fluor 0.2%), carried at no growth. **Q3 weighs against**: the roads built need little, but growth is bought at auction against funds the filer says accept lower returns (I-24 $9.2B with no service until 2034, I-285 East $8.9B); Highways about 6.2% pre-tax on the consolidated concession book; the 2025 purchase of 5.06% of 407 ETR at about a 3.4% EBITDA yield. **Q4 weighs against, not a STOP**: nine balance sheets read; equity attributable EUR 5,503M to EUR 3,187M by 2020, rebuilt by the EUR 2,570M Heathrow gain in 2024, not by retained earnings; goodwill EUR 412M; parent net cash about equal to construction's customer advances; receivables 15.5% to 18.3% of revenue; Adjusted EBITDA featured in every release, carried to Q5. **Q5 OUT on integrity, on doubt** **[M2013-088]**, **[M2007-092]**: the business decided at Q2 lives on public tenders; the CNMC resolution of 2022-07-06 "stating that it had been proven" that Ferrovial Construccion committed "a very serious infringement" in public-tender conduct, fined EUR 38.5M, suspended on appeal and not provided; a second CNMC "very serious infringement" by Ferroser (a Ferrovial company until 2022-01-31) in road-maintenance tenders, EUR 5.7M and a contracting prohibition, suspended; the February 2023 detention of the president and vice-president of FBSerwis (a Budimex subsidiary) in a bribery and tax-fraud investigation over waste tenders, both dismissed, the investigation closed as to Budimex; four Slovak environmental criminal matters at the D4R7 joint venture. The case for management written in: full disclosure, no director or executive named, prompt removal in Poland. The analyst declared the STOP on findings under appeal a departure another analyst could weigh short of closing. Q6 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop, recorded not weighed: buybacks EUR 973M in 2024 (average EUR 37.90 under the 2024 programme), EUR 501M in 2025, EUR 300M in H1 2026 at about EUR 58.31, all above the computed bottom; the del Pino family 21.87% and 8.66%, TCI 10.03%; an Executive Chairman since 2000; non-recourse project borrowings EUR 7,617M, parent net cash EUR 1,307M (June 2026); the NTO delay and its remedial plan; the Turow claim of EUR 248.2M against the Budimex consortium. Owner cash (operating cash with equity investees at dividends received, less PP&E and intangible capex, project capex, lease payments and the minority partners' dividends) 2021 to 2025 attributable: maintenance case average **EUR 638M** (project capex replaced by a EUR 50M maintenance guess, a CONVENTION of the run), all spending EUR 291M; first year aberrational, growth by the halves measure 24.8% (a CONVENTION of the run), capped under (f) at the business's own sales growth, 8.64%; a net seller, sale proceeds not credited centrally (a CONVENTION of the run). COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value range **EUR 15.41 to 41.39** a share ($17.33 to $46.54; all-equity, maintenance, attributable, at 3.67%), net debt EUR 6,283M; 1.7% to 3.5% at the price, no case earns the floor, so Q7 would have closed OUT; fair **EUR 3.76 all-equity** ($4.23; EUR 7.11 or $7.99 equity-only); not armed, the box being OUT at Q5. Contamination declared by the analyst: the TTEK commit subjects in its opening context and a memory index line; no blind-listed file opened; none used. Commits 430f9ded (template), 175396f3 (Step 0 and Q1), f7932729 (Q2), a165a5ea (Q3), c266bf72 (Q4), aec71557 (Q5), 8d44ae97 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` PASS (62 ids); the dispatcher's `fold_cite_check.py`, 17 quoted fragments beside an id, all in their rows: **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q5 on a competition authority's finding against a subsidiary, suspended by a court, no individual named, and whether integrity is read by parts or for the whole; (2) the all-equity basis with consolidated minority partners owning 27% to 46% of the concessions (fair EUR 3.76 with their dividends deducted, EUR 10.09 with them not deducted); (3) specific (a) where only one trough exists; (4) a net seller under (c), sale proceeds as negative capital spending; (5) the template's 10-K wording for a 20-F filer whose earlier balance sheets are not on EDGAR. Could not get: a maintenance split, the I-24 and I-285 equity commitments, the period of the cartel conduct, 407 ETR's 2019 traffic.
runs.narr: OUT at Q5 (Ferrovial N.V., Ferrovial SE until 2026-04-30, delisted from Euronext Amsterdam 2026-09-11; toll roads, airports, construction and energy, Highways deciding with 407 ETR at 48.3% and the US managed lanes; Heathrow and AGS sold in 2025). Q1 IN narrowly, Q2 IN on Highways (407 ETR revenue compounding 8.3% since 2009, managed-lane revenue per trip rising well above inflation), Construction an open castle; Q3 and Q4 weigh against (growth bought at auction against cheaper capital, about 6.2% pre-tax on the consolidated concession book, equity rebuilt by the Heathrow gain). Q5 OUT on doubt: two CNMC "very serious infringement" resolutions on public-tender conduct in two Ferrovial companies (EUR 38.5M and EUR 5.7M, suspended on appeal) and the 2023 bribery arrests at a Budimex subsidiary, in a business that lives on public tenders; no director named; the analyst declared the close a departure another analyst could weigh short of closing. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value EUR 15.41 to 41.39 all-equity ($17.33 to $46.54) against EUR 43.94 ($49.41), no case earning the floor, fair EUR 3.76 all-equity ($4.23), EUR 7.11 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: Q5 on findings under appeal and by parts or whole, minority partners on the all-equity basis, (a) with one trough, a net seller under (c), the template for a 20-F filer.
